paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is about: the LORD keeps His word, and He is the One who hands out the land. Esau got Mount Seir, and Lot's descendants got Ar and the land of the Ammonites, and the LORD told Israel to leave all of it alone. He said Israel would not get "not even a footprint" (Deuteronomy 2:5). The notes about the Horites, the Emites and the Zamzummites show the LORD had been giving other peoples their homes long before Israel showed up (Deuteronomy 2:12, 21-22).

That matters, because the LORD told Israel to leave alone land He had given to others. He even told them to pay in silver for the food they ate and the water they drank (Deuteronomy 2:6). The One who gave Seir to Esau is the One who decides who gets what. So you don't have to grab at what belongs to somebody else, and you can deal honestly and fairly with the people you meet.

And look at who was with them the whole time. Moses tells the people, "The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing" (Deuteronomy 2:7). Even the long wandering was under His watch, and what He swore came true (Deuteronomy 2:14). So when your own road feels long, baker, trust the One who is walking it with you, and remember the story isn't over, because Moses still has more to say.
